stories.headline: Tyreek Hill's Wagon Hits a Ditch - Dislocated Knee Leaves Miami's Passing Camp Wide Open
stories.read: Well pardner, word off Monday night's wire is that Tyreek Hill dislocated his knee, and he's likely done for the season, which makes Miami a dry well for anyone ridin' the old cheetah. But every hole in the trail's a strike for somebody: Jaylen Waddle just inherited a bigger cut of the throws, and Darren Waller scored twice in his comeback, huntin' the ball on nearly every two-tight-end snap. Doc's read: swap horses toward Waddle and Waller before the saloon catches on, and rent Nick Westbrook-Ikhine only in the deep outfits.

stories.headline: Gunslinger Graveyard - Dart Done for the Year, Caleb Williams Laid Up, Mayfield Nursin' a Thumb
stories.read: Hold up there, the quarterback corral just got thinned out something fierce. Jaxson Dart tore up his knee and is finished for 2026 with Jameis Winston takin' the reins, Caleb Williams is out three to four weeks with a hamstring strain, and Baker Mayfield's throwin' thumb is waitin' on imaging. Every pass-catcher tied to those three just lost some ceiling, so don't be the fella holdin' a dry well. Doc's read: go rent a horse on the open range and scoop the best free gunslinger before your leaguemates finish their coffee.

stories.headline: Cheap Gold on the Open Range - Gordon, Hollins and Juwan Johnson Ripe for Stakin'
stories.read: With De'Von Achane out for the year, Ollie Gordon II got all the backfield work in Miami and cashed a goal-line touchdown, yet just 1 percent of outfits have staked him. Over in New England, A.J. Brown is off the trail until mid-October, and Mack Hollins led the team with a 19.5 percent cut of the throws while only 5 percent of the saloon owns him. Saints tight end Juwan Johnson is the third-best TE through three weeks but still sits unclaimed in plenty of leagues. Doc's read: file those claims first thing, pardner, before the herd stampedes in.
